fixture: the first complete ESP32-C3 ladder rung; fixed U1 terminal to R1 pad 1, while R1 pad 2 remains intentionally unconnected
hypothesis: projected trace tension can transfer through a body-local terminal attachment and move or rotate a real KiCad footprint while preserving a complete board

controls.name: unconstrained_translation
controls.reason: one F.Silkscreen clearance violation between R1 graphics and the R2 reference field

controls.name: unconstrained_translation_and_rotation
controls.reason: one F.Silkscreen clearance violation; free rotation worked mechanically but was 0.027031 mm worse than translation-only

controls.name: one_step_translation
controls.reason: the source placement has effectively no positive-Y silkscreen margin, so reducing the step count did not repair the missing placement constraint

interpretation: Real KiCad tracer-to-placer coupling now works for one deliberately small terminal component and persists through candidate application and ladder rematerialization. Axis-constrained motion is the only accepted control and slightly outperforms the invalid higher-freedom proposals. The failed controls show that copper-only analytic obstacles are insufficient for placement: courtyard, silkscreen, and eventually body/body constraints must enter the continuous neighborhood before arbitrary motion can be committed automatically. This is not evidence that rotation is undesirable; it proves rotation is active and exposes a missing constraint family on this fixture.
